title: LA County food ownership and process changes need their own permit file
jurisdiction: City of Los Angeles / county environmental-health service
activity: Buying a restaurant or changing its equipment/menu/operation
affectedParty: Actual restaurant operating entity and owner
applicability: Only the stated jurisdiction/activity and actual facts; not overall opening clearance.
requirement: The permit application is nontransferable and tied to the named person/location/activity/time. The purchase instructions distinguish the district-office route from new/major-modification plan check; the form separately calls for review and approval of equipment/menu/operation changes. Do not equate buying equipment or submitting a form with an issued permit.
exceptions: Determine actual site, activity, category and agency scope against the current authority.
trigger: Buying a restaurant or changing its equipment/menu/operation
deadline: Resolve the applicable review/issued-record requirements before covered operation; follow an actual received notice’s due date.
renewal: Confirm current record term and recheck owner, site, process, equipment and discharge changes.
evidence: Actual municipal address and county-service authority
Actual new owner and prior facility records
Applicable reviewed application and issued health permit
interpretationLimits: No actual restaurant approval, no blanket unchanged-site exemption, and no all-county or neighbouring-city permission.
reviewerStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

title: A Los Angeles restaurant remodel joins county food review to city premises approvals
jurisdiction: City of Los Angeles / Los Angeles County
activity: New retail food facility or covered change to an existing facility
affectedParty: Food operator, plan designer and premises lead
applicability: Only the stated jurisdiction/activity and actual facts; not overall opening clearance.
requirement: County plan-check instructions call for the actual menu/equipment/plan package and separate planning/building approval, inspections, conditional health approval and issued public-health permit. Use the actual project scope and retain distinct decisions, rather than treating business tax registration as the food-opening record.
exceptions: Determine actual site, activity, category and agency scope against the current authority.
trigger: New retail food facility or covered change to an existing facility
deadline: Resolve the applicable review/issued-record requirements before covered operation; follow an actual received notice’s due date.
renewal: Confirm current record term and recheck owner, site, process, equipment and discharge changes.
evidence: Current menu, equipment schedule/specifications and scaled plans
interpretationLimits: No guaranteed fee/review time, technical design approval, alcohol/outdoor-service or actual grease/fire/accessibility determination.
reviewerStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

title: Houston distinguishes non-industrial commercial laundry from industrial-waste discharge
jurisdiction: Houston sanitary sewer / actual IWS jurisdiction
activity: Proposing a laundry discharge to the city sanitary sewer
applicability: Only the stated jurisdiction/activity and actual facts; not overall opening clearance.
requirement: Houston’s FAQ lists self-service/commercial (not industrial) laundry outside its stated Industrial Waste Permit requirement, but reserves an IWS permit determination for facilities discharging industrial waste. It directs a facility proposing non-domestic sewer discharge to contact IWS and submit the survey; that route does not depend on first receiving a mailed request. Present the actual operations/discharge facts and obtain the applicable determination, not a blanket sewer exemption.
exceptions: Determine actual site, activity, category and agency scope against the current authority.
trigger: Proposing a laundry discharge to the city sanitary sewer
deadline: Resolve the applicable review/issued-record requirements before covered operation; follow an actual received notice’s due date.
renewal: Confirm current record term and recheck owner, site, process, equipment and discharge changes.
evidence: Actual receiving sewer authority and service address
Prospective-discharge IWS contact and survey submission
IWS classification, applicable review and issued record where required
interpretationLimits: No actual non-industrial classification, numeric discharge limit, treatment design, direct-discharge or receiving-authority determination.
reviewerStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

title: A received Houston industrial-wastewater survey remains a separate response task
jurisdiction: City of Houston Industrial Wastewater Service
affectedParty: Requested facility operator and authorised signer
applicability: Only the stated jurisdiction/activity and actual facts; not overall opening clearance.
requirement: The city calls a received survey a mandatory report request and describes consequences for missing its due date. Complete the actual water-use/discharge record, sign and return it under the request; the survey is not itself an issued permit or an automatic finding that one is needed.
exceptions: Determine actual site, activity, category and agency scope against the current authority.
deadline: Resolve the applicable review/issued-record requirements before covered operation; follow an actual received notice’s due date.
renewal: Confirm current record term and recheck owner, site, process, equipment and discharge changes.
evidence: Signed response, submission record and IWS follow-up
interpretationLimits: No assertion that every commercial facility has received the survey or that survey submission completes every operating duty.
reviewerStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review
